::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 4](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/part-4-multiverse-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The last week of the last case works the largest menu of the course, fourteen decisions and a curve of 864 specifications, and asks two questions that the earlier cases met only in part: how much certainty a panel of twenty-seven countries can give, when every result is tested by a bootstrap that resamples whole countries, and what hundreds of estimates on the same data can establish when they are not independent tests. Read the menu and the decision map before the class meets. In class you explore, read the chart, and declare, run and report. The week also starts the final project: choose it from the [list of projects](week-12.qmd#the-projects) and write its preregistration, which is due at the start of week 12, before anything in it has been run.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Specification menu](../../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd) and [Decision map](../../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) | Before class. The fourteen decisions and the three levels into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps, and the alignment of every result with the direction of the claim; then every decision on the map, in the order in which an analyst meets it, with what each option does to the estimand statement and to the results. | 40 minutes |
| Slides, the menu in [Part 3](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration), and Task 4 in your report or [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore), then [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | In class. The methodological tutorial if the class wants it, then `try_spec()` one argument at a time, compared with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for pooled OLS (`estimator = "pooled_cl"`) to read why it is refused, and send the try that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`; it is drawn in green on the class chart. | 30 minutes |

The multiverse tutorial, the class chart against the curve of 864, the decision that carries the largest share of the variation across specifications, where the five reanalyses and the original study sit, your own placement on the curve, and the inference that a curve does and does not support. | 35 minutes |

Complete the block before you run anything, one option for each of the fourteen decisions, and run `prereg()`; then translate the declaration into model syntax yourself, run it, and send it with `report_result()`. It is drawn in black beside the green explorations. | 25 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-inference), standard errors with few clusters | Why ten years of one country carry less information than ten independent observations, the CR2 correction with its Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, and the restricted wild cluster bootstrap by which every point of the curve is classed. Under that bootstrap the reproduced specification has a p of 0.110, so it is not significant at 5% under the test of the curve, although its conventional p is 0.0002. | 30 minutes |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) | Description and inference, why 864 estimates on the same data are not 864 independent tests, what a permutation test of the whole curve would have to do, and what can be said without one. | 35 minutes |

| [Missing answers](../../companion/missingness.qmd) | What a respondent who mentions no frame at all does to a share built from mentions, the rules that the menu offers for such respondents and what each assumes, and multiple imputation against the rules set by fiat. | 30 minutes |
| Your report | Render the report with all five tasks complete, the preregistration as it stood before the run and the result beneath it. This is the fourth case report. | 20 minutes |

Hand it in, or register it on OSF Registries, before week 12 meets. | 60 minutes |
| Optional: [The individual level](../../companion/individual-level.qmd) and [Simulation as a method](../../companion/simulation.qmd) | The claim fitted at the level of respondents, where the original author (OA) fitted it, on a simulated person-level dataset validated against the real respondents; and data with a known recipe, in which a method can be checked against an answer known in advance. Either supports a final project on this case. | as you like |

**By the end of the session** you have your declared result placed among the 864 specifications of the curve, the fourth case report rendered, a sentence on what the bootstrap by country changes for the reproduced specification, and the preregistration of your final project written and handed in before week 12.
